rationale:
Issue #147 (labeled 'bug', opened 2024-01-27, well before the fix) names the exact defective expression `uri = "\(scheme)://\(host)\(relativePath)\(port)"` and reports it yields invalid targets such as `wss://apple.com/asdf:55433`, proposing host-then-port ordering. The minimized production patch is that identical single-line reorder in Sources/WebSocketKit/WebSocketClient.swift, and the trigger test testProxy asserts the request head URI is `ws://apple.com:<port>/` instead of the previously encoded buggy `ws://apple.com/:<port>` — issue, trigger, and fix describe one pre-existing proxy URI construction defect. The minimized patch is 1 of 1 production hunks (original_hunk_count=1, removed_hunk_count=0, post_minimization_validation=PASS) and contains only the interpolation reorder: no refactor, formatting, feature, docs, config, or test change; the other PR #160 commits (configuration forwarding, wss origin-form) are excluded from this revision pair. The trigger is the upstream test-side counterpart of the same commit with only a diagnostic-shape reduction (XCTAssertEqual(a, b) to XCTAssertTrue(a == b)) per trigger_reduction, preserving the exact URI equality condition, the dynamically bound local port, and the network path; it exercises only pre-existing symbols (scheme, host, proxyPort, path, HTTPRequestHead.uri) and depends on no API introduced by the fix. Strict machine evidence passes on both the original and post-minimization matrices: build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential (reproduced selector testProxy), trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups), trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green, over 32 runs with 3 repetitions and no failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and vapor/websocket-kit#147 is the sole allowed verified issue key, so no duplicate root cause exists.

The minimized production patch is a single one-line hunk in Sources/WebSocketKit/WebSocketClient.swift reordering the interpolation to `\(host)\(port)\(relativePath)`; there is no refactor, formatting, feature, docs, or config change, and the two sibling concerns from PR #160 (passing `configuration` through the proxy path, wss origin-form URI) live in separate commits and are absent here. The trigger is the pre-existing testProxy whose assertion previously encoded the defective format `ws://apple.com/:<port>` and now asserts `ws://apple.com:<port>/`; the curator variant only swaps XCTAssertEqual for XCTAssertTrue on the identical equality condition to suppress ephemeral-port diagnostic text, so the pass/fail semantics are unchanged, and it references only symbols (host, proxyPort, relativePath, scheme) already present at the buggy revision, so no new production API is required. Machine-generated strict evidence passes on both the original and post-minimization runs: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (1/1), trigger.buggy_differential reproducing Tests/WebSocketKitTests/WebSocketKitTests.swift::testProxy, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic across 3 repetitions with 32 matrix runs, and full_suite.fixed_all_green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and vapor/websocket-kit#147 is the sole allowed verified issue key, so no duplicate root cause exists.

testProxy uses the literal hostname 'apple.com' as the CONNECT target against a local WebsocketBin stub; if the stub ever forwards instead of short-circuiting, the trigger could touch the network, though 3-repetition determinism and fixed-clean runs passed.
The trigger asserts only the root path with a bound proxy port; non-root paths and the proxyPort == nil branch of the same expression are not covered.

The wss/proxy origin-form and configuration-forwarding defects described in PR #160 remain present at the fixed revision, so this case isolates only the URI ordering aspect of the issue title 'WSS Proxy Setup Broken'.
Trigger relies on force-unwrapped ctx.localAddress!.port!, which would crash rather than fail cleanly under adverse scheduling.
